main_text.p: Ne forté incidas in laqueos illius) id eft, fraudibus & concupiscentijs capiaris, per fi-gna lasciuiae tibi oftenfa. Inuenit enim Eccle-siastes mulierem amariorem morte, & quod laqueus eft venatoris, & sagena cor eius, & vincula sunt manus eius. vnde & Diogenes, animaduertens Olympionicem quendam oculos defigere in scortum, adeo vt praeteri-tum capite reflexo intueretur: Ecce vt, in-quit, aries Martius à puella publica, obtorto collo vinctus abducitur. Ridiculum exifti-mabat, certare cum electis viris, & à vili pu-ella veluti captiuum trahi sine funibus. Rec-tius igitur Alexander Magnus, quum inui-taretur vt Darij filias quas habebat captiuas inuiferet: praedicabantur .n. puellae admira-bili esse forma, noluit ire, dicens, sibi non committendum, vt quum viros vicisset, à mulieribus vinceretur.

Cum afsiduus fis: nec audias illam, ne forté pereas in efficacia illius) vel, vt Græcus habet: μὴ ψαλλούσης μὴ ἐνδελχίζῃς, μὴ τρο-τὶ ἄλλως ἐν τοῖς ἐπιχειρήμασιν ἀνῆς.[?] Saltatricem vocat (inquit Pellicanus) cum lasciuia & pe-tulanter ftudioseque choreis assuetam, huiusmodi vitandam ac fugiendam docet: ge-stu enim, aspectu & tactu, alloquio & cantu prouocat ad libidinem. Tali Herodiadis fi-lia captus est improbus alioqui rex Herodes, vt Baptistam Ioannem decollari praeceperit. Sara autem Tobiae iunioris vxor: Tu, inquit, scis Domine, quod nunquam concu-ui[?] vi-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Rectius" is read from the hyphenated "Re-" at the line end and the ligature in "ftius". The Greek phrase at the foot of the second paragraph is hard to read, especially the words after "τρο-" and the final word, and is marked [?]. The word after "concu-" at the foot of the page is partly unclear and is marked [?]. The page number reads "814" (set as "ʂ14"). The spelling "afsiduus" and "Ecclesiastes" follows the printed form with long s rendered as plain s.
